verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:

verses.english: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, they speak of this thing called ‘ignorance’.
And how is an ignoramus defined?”

verses.pali: “Idhāvuso, assutavā puthujjano rūpaṁ nappajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ nappajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: “Reverend, it’s when an unlearned ordinary person doesn’t understand form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ nappajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
And this is how an ignoramus is defined.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to him:
“Reverend Koṭṭhita, they speak of this thing called ‘knowledge’.
And how is a knowing one defined?”

verses.pali: “Idhāvuso, sutavā ariyasāvako rūpaṁ pajānāti, rūpasamudayaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhaṁ pajānāti, rūpanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: “Reverend, it’s when a learned noble disciple understands form, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇasamudayaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhaṁ pajānāti, viññāṇanirodhagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: consciousness, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation.
And this is how a knowing one is defined.”
